solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Horny old beast put in A&E by one serving unbeatably on team?

indicators.note: the answer is what you would put between an A and an E, so the wordplay's outer A and E must come off to leave it

parts.note: a tennis player who serves aces, shots the receiver cannot return
atop means on, resting on top of
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A randy dinosaur is rushed to casualty by a tennis ace from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer is what you would put inside an A and an E to spell the wordplay. A&E is a British hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceratopsids are the extinct horned dinosaurs such as Triceratops, so a prehistoric creature bearing horns.

clue.text: Gem cut at top and six-pack comprising Mike's dearest possessions

indicators.note: comprising means including, so the six-pack word holds the letter for Mike inside it
cutting at the top lops off the first letter of the gem word

parts.note: a jewel is a gem
a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, or abs
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike prizes his cut gems and his toned stomach above everything.
explanation.walkthrough: JEWEL loses its J, then ABS takes M in to make AMBS: EWE-LAMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: From Nathan's parable of the poor man's one treasured ewe lamb, the phrase means someone's most cherished possession.

clue.text: Sweet-tasting fish a second person starved of oxygen

indicators.note: starved of means deprived of, so the chemical symbol for oxygen is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A tasty fish, and someone else gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the symbol for oxygen, so A YOU drops its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The ayu is a small Japanese river fish, also called sweetfish for the delicate flavour of its flesh.

clue.text: Raise grand in shared currency for multibarrelled shooter

indicators.note: in a down clue raising something lifts it, so the letters read upwards
in places the letter for grand inside the currency word

parts.note: the euro is the currency shared by many EU countries
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone raising a thousand in euros to buy a gun with many barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside EURO as EU-G-RO, which read upwards in the grid gives ORGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgue, or organ gun, was an old weapon with several barrels in a row, like the pipes of an organ.

clue.text: Ancient form of document left in county to the north and east

indicators.note: in sets the letter for left inside the other pieces
in a down entry going north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county
L is the usual abbreviation for left
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An old document from a county up north and to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire is an English county; the reversed county and east are joined, and left slips in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrowle is an obsolete spelling of scroll, a rolled written record of the sort once used for deeds.

clue.text: Creator god protects fighter circling Sumerian city

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the god word wraps round the rest

parts.note: deus is Latin for god

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the fighter word encloses the city

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
Ur was a city of ancient Sumer

explanation.surface: A deity keeps a warplane safe as it flies around an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creator god' reads as one phrase, but only the first word is the definition; the god is Latin and does the protecting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic and Gnostic thought the demiurge is the maker who fashions the physical world.

clue.text: Islamic judge's bit of publicity in show of surprising facts

indicators.note: in puts the publicity word inside the letters naming the show

parts.note: QI is a BBC quiz show built on unusual and surprising facts
an ad is a small piece of advertising

explanation.surface: A Muslim judge makes a brief promotional appearance on a trivia programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A qadi is a judge in a Muslim court who rules according to sharia law.

clue.text: Ruler used to circumscribe radius and clip one's beak

indicators.note: to circumscribe is to draw a line all the way round, so the ruler word encloses what follows

parts.note: a queen is a ruler
r is the standard symbol for radius
to cuff is to clip someone round the ear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monarch measures a circle's radius, then smacks someone's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' looks like a bird's bill, but in British slang a beak is a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer cuffin is old thieves' cant for a justice of the peace, and a beak is British slang for such a magistrate.

clue.text: Aperitif, extremely fine to be imbibed by thirsty good-for-nothing

indicators.note: something imbibed is swallowed, so it ends up inside the thirsty word

parts.note: dry means thirsty

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of the drink word

parts.note: the first and last letters of aperitif
F stands for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A thirsty layabout downs an aperitif, which turns out very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Draffy means worthless, from draff, the dregs or refuse left after brewing, as good for nothing as such waste.

clue.text: Begrudge developing tool for improving software

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of the first word grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A programmer resents having to work on a tool that fixes code.
explanation.definitionFit: A debugger is a program used to find and remove errors in other programs.

clue.text: Old lady recalled European woman frequenting orgies

parts.note: one's old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the European word is read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A mother remembers a Danish woman who went to wild parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the frenzied female followers of Dionysus, whose rites were famous for drunken revelry.

clue.text: Australian nipper back in the same place in auction site

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse
in places the abbreviation for the same place inside the auction site's name

parts.note: eBay is the online auction site
ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: An Australian child is back where they were, on an auction website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' looks like a child but means a creature that nips. Ib. is a footnote convention for a source just cited.
explanation.definitionFit: A yabbie is an Australian freshwater crayfish, and its claws give a painful pinch.

clue.text: Board accepting bit of work on school drive's deep crack in ice

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the board abbreviation holds the following pieces

parts.note: bd is an abbreviation for board
an erg is a small unit of work in physics
sch is the abbreviation for school
to run a machine is to drive it

explanation.surface: An education board takes on work at a school with real drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bergschrund is the gaping crevasse where a glacier pulls away from the steeper ice or rock above it.

clue.text: Hostilities engulfing Britain whenever English and Scottish on the alert

definitions.note: Scottish marks the word as Scots

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the hostilities word surrounds Britain's abbreviation

parts.note: hostilities amount to war
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain
if can mean whenever, as in if it rains, I stay in
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: In wartime the British stay watchful, the English as much as the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Waukrife is a Scots word for wakeful or watchful, unable to sleep and alert to danger.

clue.text: Honour someone striking gold with gram in Bavarian village

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
a rammer is one who rams or strikes
g is the symbol for gram
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An honoured prospector strikes gold, measured by the gram, in a German village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold with gram' puts G beside AU, and G comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberammergau is the village in Bavaria famous for its Passion Play, staged every ten years.

clue.text: Greek character following more commendable Echo is captured by Castor

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so the Echo letter sits within the comparative

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
f is the abbreviation for following, as in p. 3f
finer means better, more worthy of praise
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Castor, one of the Greek twins of myth, captures a nymph called Echo.
explanation.walkthrough: Castor looks like the mythical twin but is a variant spelling of caster, a sugar or spice shaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffineer is a shaker with a perforated lid for sprinkling sugar or spice on muffins, i.e. a caster.

clue.text: Boyfriend has local cheat to carry a torch

parts.note: flam is a dialect word for a sham or a trick
a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: A woman's boyfriend has been cheating on her, yet she still pines for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry a torch' suggests unrequited love, but the torch is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of several thick wax wicks.

clue.text: Careful with sauce covering paper and disinfectant doing the same

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the sauce word goes round everything after it

parts.note: soy is a sauce
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

indicators.note: doing the same repeats the covering, so the disinfectant also wraps round the paper

parts.note: Lysol is a brand of disinfectant
the paper is used a second time

explanation.surface: A cook carefully pours sauce over paper and then does the same with disinfectant.
explanation.walkthrough: The containers nest: the sauce wraps everything, and the disinfectant inside it wraps a second copy of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Softly-softly describes a cautious, patient approach, from the saying softly softly catchee monkey.

clue.text: Salyut's middle level involves senior Soviet scientist

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the senior abbreviation goes inside
middle asks for the central letters of the space station's name

parts.note: the two central letters of Salyut, a Soviet space station
sen is the abbreviation for senior
to KO, knock out, someone is to level or floor them

explanation.surface: A senior Soviet scientist works on the middle deck of the Salyut space station.
explanation.definitionFit: Trofim Lysenko was the Soviet biologist whose discredited genetics theories Stalin backed.

clue.text: Sodden chamber giving nonstop pain

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
achy describes a dull pain that goes on and on

explanation.surface: A damp room where someone suffers constant aches.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamber means a chamber pot, which British slang shortens to po.
explanation.definitionFit: Poachy describes ground that is wet and soft, easily trampled into mud by livestock.

clue.text: Foot bones start to hurt less when November's gone

indicators.note: gone means removed, so the letter for November is taken out

parts.note: Bones, or sawbones, is slang for a doctor, a doc

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of hurt

parts.note: first letter of hurt
less means minus, as in five less two
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The bones in your foot start to hurt less after November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' wants to be the body part with bones; it is a unit of poetic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A dochmius is a metrical unit, a five-syllable foot used in Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Gum resin mastic on images' frames

indicators.note: the phrase frames the answer, holding it inside like a picture in a frame

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Mastic, itself a gum resin, has been smeared on the frames of pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastic is a gum resin too, so it looks like the definition; the answer is inside masTIC ON IMAges.
explanation.definitionFit: Conima is a fragrant resin from a tropical American tree, burned as incense.

clue.text: Modern dance clubs with revolutionary ending in popular music

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the music ending is flipped round

parts.note: -core ends the names of many popular music styles, such as hardcore, grindcore and emocore

explanation.surface: Dance clubs adopt a radical finale for their pop music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceroc is a partner dance style that began in 1980s London, blending jive and salsa.

clue.text: Bulk needing one to change to vineyard's disused press

indicators.note: change to means swap, so the letter for one gives way to the vineyard word

parts.note: bulk is size
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cru is a vineyard, as in grand cru

explanation.surface: A large old wine press needs one part replacing at the vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruze is an obsolete word for squeeze or press, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Secure what holds edges of railing for water pipe

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so the securing word wraps round the railing letters

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it

indicators.note: edges of means the first and last letters of railing

parts.note: the first and last letters of railing
eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what will keep a railing in place for a water pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The secure word NAIL holds RG; 'what' gives EH, added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargileh is an oriental tobacco pipe that draws smoke through water, a hookah.

clue.text: Ruling party members regularly rejected Zionism

indicators.note: every other letter is rejected in a regular pattern, leaving the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters, once the first, third, fifth and seventh are thrown out

explanation.surface: The governing party's members have turned against Zionism.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins are those in office, the party currently holding power, as opposed to the outs.

clue.text: Crossbar in support of millstone's outer edge's sound

indicators.note: sound tells you the word is heard rather than seen, so match its pronunciation

parts.note: rind is the outer edge or skin of something like cheese or bacon

explanation.surface: A crossbar keeps the rim of a millstone in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A rynd is the iron fitting across the eye of an upper millstone that carries its weight on the spindle.

clue.text: Gardening charity crossing over here to Nancy with shady evergeen climber

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the charity's letters span the pieces after it

parts.note: the RHS is the Royal Horticultural Society, a British gardening charity
o is the cricket abbreviation for over
ici is French for here, and Nancy is a French city
sus is slang for suspicious, shady

explanation.surface: A gardening charity sends someone over to France with a vine for shady spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Shady looks like part of the definition, describing where the climber grows, but it gives SUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoicissus is a genus of evergreen vines from Africa, grown as house plants such as the grape ivy.
